description: Hunt for a flaky integration test: timing dependence, shared-runner port collisions, test ordering and a fixture that leaks state between cases.

facts.statement: The shared runner log showed the flaky integration-test database configuration file at /home/runner/work/payment-api/.ci/integration-db.yaml.
The shared runner's cgroup memory limit was recorded as 4294967296 bytes while investigating the flaky integration test.
The shared runner's Docker Compose file pins the flaky integration test's mock OAuth server to host TCP port 49221.
The shared-runner retry wrapper logged `attempt=3/3` when the flaky integration test failed.
The shared-runner-only flaky integration test was traced to commit prefix a13f9d.
During the CI investigation, the shared-runner integration job measured 4 minutes 30 seconds longer than the self-hosted baseline.
During the shared-runner integration investigation, we ran pytest with the command-line flag `--randomly-seed=0` to force a fixed test order.
The flaky integration test only failed on the shared runner because its artifact upload step targeted the S3 bucket `ci-shared-runner-flaky-artifacts`.
The shared runner lockfile pins testcontainers-core to version 1.19.8 in the flaky integration test investigation.
The function that guards the shared-runner cache during the flaky integration test is `acquireSharedRunnerCacheLock`.
The flaky integration test writes its temporary rows into the `shared_runner_flaky_tmp` schema.
The shared runner wrote the flaky integration report to /home/ci/shared-runner.xml.

messages.text: Make the flaky integration test deterministic without disabling it.

Shared runner: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15.0-104, Node 18.19.1, npm 10.2.4. The test payments/checkout_spec.py calls get_payment_gateway_client() and reads PAYER_API_BASE_URL. On this runner that env var is empty, so it falls back to http://localhost:3000. Port 3000 is occupied by runner-agent, not the mock API, and the traceback hits checkout_spec.py line 87 expecting 200 but getting 502.

The next file I want to open is .github/workflows/integration.yml, specifically around lines 92–118, because the failure is runner-local and the test itself passed in my local run. I need to compare the shared-runner invocation with the self-hosted job: the job name is integration-shared-runner, the pytest step uses python -m pytest -q --maxfail=1 --junitxml=reports/integration.xml tests/integration/test_pipeline_upload.py with no retry or timeout wrapper, and timeout-minutes: 10 may be too close to the observed 9m42s elapsed time. I also want to inspect the env block near line 103 for CI=true, RUNNER_DEBUG=1, TMPDIR=/mnt/runner-ephemeral, and API_BASE_URL=https://staging.example.internal, because shared runners may expose different network or tmpfs behavior. If the workflow passes --reruns=2 only on the non-shared job, that would explain why only shared runs intermittently show the failure; if not, I will move to tests/integration/conftest.py line 44, where the shared fixture creates the temporary workspace and may leak state between concurrent jobs on the same runner.

New scope: stop debugging test ordering and inspect why the shared runner lacks DOCKER_HOST and has PATH order for Node 20 vs 18; compare /opt/actions-runner/_work/.env and node --version in integration.yml before pytest-integration, then add runner label checks to .github/workflows/integration.yml.

Given the failure appears only on the shared runner, I will inspect `.github/workflows/integration.yml` next, specifically lines 48–71 where the job launches `postgres:15.3-alpine` with `--health-cmd pg_isready` and maps host port 5432. I want to verify whether the shared runner reuses that port, adds `NODE_ENV=test` inconsistently, or sets `TEST_DATABASE_URL` from the matrix rather than the ephemeral service. If the service container is not `docker` or uses `ubuntu-latest` instead of `self-hosted` image, network isolation and mount paths could differ. I will also compare the `timeout-minutes: 10` and `continue-on-error: true` flag to explain why flakiness is masked locally but surfaces on the runner. No fix yet; this should confirm whether the shared runner environment, not the assertion, is the source.

New symptom: on shared runner, after upgrading Node 20.15.1 to 20.16.0, tests/api/profile.spec.ts flakes with ECONNRESET in axios.get, only when CI=true and AWS_REGION=us-east-1. Stack points to node:http Socket.close at lib/internal/streams/readable.js:823 and node_modules/axios/dist/node/axios.cjs:1657. Locally with node --no-warnings passes; retrying the job once usually fixes it.

Looking at the flake, integration:api-rate-limit fails only on the shared runner ubuntu-latest at line 88 of .github/workflows/integration.yml, while passing on self-hosted runners. The shared runner is CPU throttled under parallel jobs, so the sidecar starts after the 10s healthcheck timeout. Minimal fix: replace the fixed sleep 5 before pnpm test:integration with a bounded readiness wait, and raise only the rate-limit suite timeout from 10s to 30s in tests/integration/rate-limit.test.ts line 12 using test.setTimeout(30_000). Also add --workers=1 to the failing suite command on line 91 to prevent container contention. This is scoped to the shared runner flake, avoids changing product code, and makes the failure deterministic by eliminating startup race rather than masking it with retries.

Please verify your previous claim that the flaky test failure in tests/integration/test_payment_runner.py comes from shared-runner env drift, not code: run pytest tests/integration/test_payment_runner.py::test_timeout -vv --log-level=DEBUG on runner tag shared with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and show whether pytest-xdist==3.5.0 and CI_DB_URL point at the same staging DB.

The shared runner log showed the flaky integration-test database configuration file at /home/runner/work/payment-api/.ci/integration-db.yaml.

The failure is in tests/integration/test_billing_webhook.sh at line 42: it calls curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health after starting the service, but the shared runner has a slower container startup than the local runner, so the first health probe often runs before the API is listening. The minimal fix is not to sleep longer globally, but to replace line 42 with a bounded readiness wait that uses the same port and fails fast if the service never becomes healthy. Change it to: for i in $(seq 1 20); do if curl -fsS --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:8080/health >/dev/null; then break; fi; sleep 1; done || { cat /tmp/billing.log; exit 1; }. This keeps CI under about 20s, avoids the flaky race, and preserves failure diagnostics. If the runner is using Docker 24.0.7, also add --health-interval=2s to the compose up step in .github/workflows/integration.yml line 19 so container health checks poll more frequently than the default 30s.

My hypothesis is shared-runner clock drift or CPU throttling makes the fixed 31-second sleep in pytest 8.1 on Python 3.11 execute during a window where the auth service’s 30-second lease is considered still valid by one clock but expired by another. The local runner passed because it is idle; shared runners show 20-second throttling and possible NTP offset. To confirm, rerun the failing commit with RUNNER_DEBUG=1 and --log-cli-level=DEBUG, then temporarily log time.monotonic(), datetime.now(timezone.utc), and auth-service /debug/clock around line 138. If failures correlate with ntp offset >0.5s, cgroup cpu.stat throttled_usec, or a gap >1s between monotonic and wall clock, that confirms it.

The log shows the test started at 09:41:27 UTC on ci-runner-07, used PostgreSQL 15.6 and the --no-cache flag for the Docker build, while successful runs were on ci-runner-02/03 with cached images. The failure message is still “timed out after 30000ms”, but the stack now includes rails test:run --seed=20240612 and tests/support/db_helpers.rb:73, where the helper sleeps 200ms between polling attempts. That suggests the shared runner is contending on the database or socket path /tmp/runner/.pg.sock, causing latency rather than a logic error. The timing distribution in the last three runs—28.9s, 30.0s, 30.1s—supports a borderline flake under load, not a broken code path.

I think the next file to inspect is .ci/docker-compose.ci.yml, not the Python test itself, because the failure only occurs on the shared runner and the test passes locally and on the self-hosted runner. The shared workflow in .github/workflows/integration-ci.yml lines 34-41 uses ubuntu-latest with runner.tags = ci-shared, and it starts postgres:16.2 and redis:7.2.3 via the compose file. On a shared runner, host ports are often occupied by previous jobs, so I want to verify whether postgres uses ports: - '5432:5432' or - '${POSTGRES_PORT}:5432', and whether the api service waits for healthcheck or only depends_on. The compose file around lines 12-27 may show no start_period or no condition: service_healthy, which would explain intermittent connection refused from app/services/clients.py:58. I also want to compare --health-cmd flags and network isolation, since shared runners reuse container networks and can leak environment variables like DATABASE_URL from prior jobs.

Under xdist, two workers can race the same port, and on the runner `localhost` may resolve to IPv6 `::1` while the server binds IPv4. Minimal fix: change the fixture to bind `127.0.0.1:0`, get the real port from the socket, and export `PAYMENT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` to the subprocess. No production or runner changes needed.

The proposed fix is to raise the wait_for_container timeout in tests/integration/test_service_health.py from 30s to 120s and add --retries=2 to the pytest invocation in .github/workflows/integration.yml around line 57. That may make the job pass, but it risks masking the actual ordering failure. The shared runner is already running postgres:16.2 and redis:7.2 in parallel, and logs show test_service_startup.py:118 can proceed before the compose healthcheck reports healthy. If we only retry or extend the sleep, the flaky race stays in the suite, and CI can start consuming extra runner minutes on every unrelated failure. There is also a side effect around line 62, where removing concurrency: group: integration-${{ github.ref }} would serialize jobs and hide cross-branch cache contention in actions/cache@v4 with key: node-20.11.1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}. This makes failures less visible rather than proving the dependency startup race is fixed.

It hits database_pool.get_conn in app/db.py, and CI env DB_URL points to ephemeral Postgres 16. I saw a TimeoutError at pytest fixture setup, so likely DB warmup race, not code path.

I’d inspect `ci/integration-pipeline.yml` next, specifically lines 42–58 where the shared-runner job starts Postgres via `services: postgres:16` and then invokes `pytest tests/integration -m integration --random-order`. Since the failure is only on the shared runner, the next most likely differentiator is runner-level environment rather than the assertion itself: concurrency, ephemeral `/tmp` limits, port collision, or service warm-up timing. That file will show whether the workflow uses `options: --health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 10s` or just a fixed `sleep`, and whether `TMPDIR`, `HOME`, or `POSTGRES_PORT` are overridden by the runner image. It also reveals if `timeout-minutes` or `continue-on-error` masks cleanup race conditions. If the workflow lacks health checks or pins no port, I can then narrow to `tests/integration/conftest.py` and the database fixture. I’m not concluding the fix yet; first confirm whether the shared runner supplies a different image tag or concurrency group than the self-hosted/ephemeral runners.

The shared runner is ubuntu-22.04, Node 20.11.1, Docker 24.0.7, CI=true. In tests/integration/order_service.spec.ts, getDBHost() reads DATABASE_HOST, but the shared runner sets DATABASE_HOST=localhost instead of postgres.service. The Postgres container uses POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret and pg_isready returns 0. Can you adjust the setup to use the service hostname?

I’m ruling out the previously suspected stale Node module cache on shared-runner-07 as the cause. I compared the failing run 54321 against three green self-hosted runner logs: the checkout step at .github/workflows/integration.yml:38 uses actions/checkout@v4 with clean: true, and the cache key for node_modules is based on the package-lock.json SHA256 plus Node 20.18.1, not the branch or timestamp, so both runners fetched the identical archive. To remove doubt, I reran the job on shared-runner-07 with actions/cache disabled, then manually deleted /home/runner/.npm_cache and ./node_modules before running npm ci --cache /tmp/empty-cache --prefer-offline=false. The test still failed in tests/integration/order_flow_it.py:147 with the same 500 from OrderService.create at src/services/order-service.ts:212, while the assertion at order_flow_it.py:163 timed out after 15s. That means the dependency snapshot is not responsible; the flake must be downstream, likely tied to the shared runner’s external postgres or docker network state.

    Sets RANDOM_SEED=482119 only for matrix entry runner=shared to

    failed with TimeoutError: gateway callback not received in 142.8s;
    seedless dedicated runs passed 2 of 3.

It fails only on the shared Linux runner, not local macOS or the dedicated runner. In .github/workflows/integration.yml, ./scripts/run_integration.sh sets CI=true and POSTGRES_HOST=postgres:5432. TestUserSessionRefresh in api/auth_test.go:118 fails after sql.DB.PingContext returns driver: bad connection.

The shared-runner-only failure points to host contention rather than application logic. On the self-hosted pool, ubuntu-22.04 runner images often leave prior jobs’ node containers or docker-proxy listeners on 127.0.0.1:3000, so tests/integration/api_health.spec.ts:47 (waitForPort(3000)) can connect to the wrong process, or startServer() at src/test/helpers/server.ts:61 gets EADDRINUSE and the assertion fails before the app routes are ready. The minimal fix is to stop using a fixed port and bind to port: 0, then pass the actual listener port into the client: const server = await startServer({ port: 0 }); const port = (server.address() as AddressInfo).port; await request(app).get('/health').expect(200);. Import AddressInfo from net. Also call server.close() in afterEach and add .unref() to timers so the runner can reclaim the process. This removes cross-job port collisions and the 5000 ms wait-on timeout becomes irrelevant.

I compared .github/workflows/integration.yml and confirmed the job does not set --rm on the container, and CI=true is present but no explicit port is passed; port discovery uses docker port near line 92. The failing output has connection reset during the first migration, which points to either stale DB state, port collision, or runner disk/CPU contention. Remaining unknown: whether the shared runner is reusing containers between unrelated matrix jobs, and whether GOFLAGS=-mod=mod plus Docker networking mode host is enabled in the runner defaults.

Test tests/integration/user_checkout_test.go::TestCheckoutWithCoupon times out in CheckoutClient.WaitForPayment at services/payment/grpc.go:118. I’ve narrowed the failure to the shared-runner branch of .github/workflows/integration.yml, lines 42–67, where the postgres:14.2 service starts with POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust and a healthcheck timeout of 30s on ubuntu-22.04. Local containers using test/integration-compose.yml pass because the app connects via localhost:5432, while the runner uses 127.0.0.1:5432 inside the job network. Logs show tests/integration/test_user_signup_flow.py:88 asserting HTTP 201 but intermittently receiving 503 after app/db.py:112 returns None from pool.acquire(). I added --timeout=30 to pytest; it did not trigger, so this is not a hung subprocess. The remaining unknown is whether the shared runner’s kernel/iptables NAT path, the postgres:14.2 initdb timing, or the pool warmup order makes the first request miss the DB. Shared-runner logs truncate before the second DB request, so I cannot tell if /var/log/postgresql/14-main.log reports ready_for_connections before or after the 503.

During the shared-runner integration investigation, we ran pytest with the command-line flag `--randomly-seed=0` to force a fixed test order.

Scope change: stop narrowing to tests/test_payment_flow.py::test_refund and check the shared runner environment itself. Compare CI_JOB_ID, RUNNER_NAME, and /etc/hosts on ubuntu-latest vs self-hosted, and inspect setup.py, pytest.ini, and docker-compose.override.yml for port collisions causing ConnectionRefusedError in requests/adapters.py:501.

The last tool output implies the shared runner is losing the race before the Postgres container becomes usable, not that the application code changed. In ci/logs/runner-ubuntu-2204-20240517.log lines 1180–1205, the integration suite starts tests/integration/payment_api_test.py:213 while docker compose is still waiting on postgres:16.2 healthcheck; the first failure is connection refused from PaymentGatewayClient.ensure_ready(). The shared runner is a Linux x86_64 Docker image python:3.11-slim, CI=true, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, TZ=UTC, but /etc/localtime is stale. The failure is in tests/integration/test_payments_flow.py::test_charge_refund at line 142, AssertionError: expected 200 got 503 from app/api/payments.py:refund(). Runner logs show pytest -k test_charge_refund --capture=no. It passes locally on macOS 14.4 with pytest 7.4.4.

The last tool output implies the failure is runner-specific rather than a deterministic logic error in the test itself. In the CI log, `integration/payment_gateway.spec.ts` timed out after 30s only on the shared `ubuntu-24.04-8-core` runner, while the same commit was green on the local Docker runner and on `ubuntu-22.04` hosted runners. The stack trace points to `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` at line 57, followed by Playwright v1.47.2 reporting `page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`. The shared-runner output also shows `curl https://localhost:8080/health` returning HTTP 503 repeatedly until after the first request attempt, suggesting the embedded mock server or Docker healthcheck is slower to become ready there. That timing skew, plus the runner’s lower available CPU/memory headroom and the default `--workers=auto` setting, makes race conditions around service startup the most plausible cause. The logs do not yet prove whether the root cause is port contention, cold-start latency, a throttled cgroup, or an environment-dependent dependency, so I should not conclude a fix from this output alone.

The flaky integration test only failed on the shared runner because its artifact upload step targeted the S3 bucket `ci-shared-runner-flaky-artifacts`.

Here's the runner-only failure:
AssertionError: expected status_code 200, got 503 in tests/integration/test_checkout_flow.py::test_reserve_inventory, at src/services/inventory_client.py:120. Shared runner uses GH_RUNNER_ID=ubuntu-latest-482, PYTHON_VERSION=3.11.8, POSTGRES_HOST=postgres:5432. Please inspect logs and add retry/debug around _make_request.

The proposed fix in `.github/workflows/integration.yml:7-10` adds `concurrency: group: integration-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` to stop parallel jobs on the self-hosted runner label `ci-shared-ubuntu22.04`. That reduces the chance that two `pytest==8.3.2` runs bind the same dynamic port from `tests/integration/test_api_health.py:84`, where `wait_for_server()` polls `http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health`. But it is a mitigation, not a guarantee: if another workflow, a cron job, or an interactive developer uses the same runner outside this concurrency group, the port collision remains. The bigger side effect is `cancel-in-progress: true`: pushing a second commit to the same branch will kill the first integration job, so we lose early feedback and may understate flakiness because a run that would have failed can be replaced before artifacts are collected. It also serializes integration coverage across PRs, lengthening queue time on the shared runner. If the intended root cause is runner contention from `actions/setup-python@v5` plus `uvicorn==0.30.1` startup latency, this fix can mask it by lowering observed frequency while increasing total CI wall time from about 3m to 8m when two or more PRs are open.

Here is the CI failure from the shared runner: tests/integration/test_payment_gateway.py::test_webhook_timeout failed with AssertionError: expected 200, got 503 after 3 retries at src/webhooks/retry_handler.py:142 in _send_with_backoff. Env: CI_RUNNER_ID=gha-shared-7, PAYGATE_TIMEOUT_MS=2000, PYTHON_VERSION=3.11.9. Repro command: pytest -q --maxfail=1.

The last tool output implies the flake is environmental rather than deterministic. In run 481293, `tests/integration/orders_test.py:212` failed at `assert wait_for_port(5432, timeout=15)` only on the shared Linux runner `ubuntu-24.04`; the same commit passed locally under Python 3.12.4 and PostgreSQL client 16.3. The runner log shows `docker: Error response from daemon: driver failed programming external connectivity` for `api_container`, and `ss -lntp` already had `0.0.0.0:8080` bound by a previous `runner-ephemeral` process. That points to port/health-check race or leftover containers from concurrent jobs, not necessarily test logic. I should correlate `GITHUB_RUN_ID` across logs, check the `--rm` and `--publish` flags in `docker-compose.yml:18`, and inspect the shared runner's cleanup hook before changing assertions.

I’m focusing on test_checkout_payment in tests/integration/checkout_payment_test.py:142, which intermittently fails only on the shared self-hosted runner in build #4821 with grpc status DeadlineExceeded after 5000 ms. The runner is ubuntu-22.04, Go 1.22.4, grpc-go v1.64.0, Docker 26.1.3, kernel 5.15.0-119. The test dials grpc.Dial("localhost:50051", grpc.WithBlock(), grpc.WithTimeout(5*time.Second)), while docker-compose.yml:77 exposes the mock payment container to 127.0.0.1:50051 and does not bind ::1. My hypothesis is that on the shared runner localhost resolves to ::1 first, and the IPv6 connect attempt hangs or races until the deadline, whereas hosted runners use IPv4-only /etc/hosts ordering. This would explain why it is runner-specific and flaky rather than deterministic. To confirm it, I would capture getent ahosts localhost, ss -ltnp, and /etc/resolv.conf on failed and green runs, then rerun the test with the dial target changed to 127.0.0.1:50051 and with GODEBUG=netdns=go+1, GRPC_VERBOSITY=DEBUG, GRPC_TRACE=client_channel,http2. If forcing IPv4 removes the DeadlineExceeded and DEBUG logs show the channel attempting [::1]:50051, the hypothesis is confirmed.

If we hide the symptom with retries, the same latent flakiness can still leak into the nightly E2E pipeline, where retries are disabled, and it may delay legitimate failures behind the 15-second budget. Another side effect is longer wall-clock time: every retry can add up to 30 seconds per test when the queue is already saturated, pushing the workflow from the current ~6 min toward 12 min on the shared runner. That removes the earlier theory that runner drift or a mixed UTC/local `created_at` serialization was causing the flake. The failing case is tests/integration/test_payment_gateway.rb:TestPaymentGateway#test_create_charge. It only fails on the shared Jenkins runner: Ubuntu 22.04, Docker 24.0.7, RAILS_ENV=test, Postgres 14-alpine. Last green commit was 7f2b1c. Logs show Timeout::Error from Net::HTTP#request at app/services/payment_gateway.rb:112.

I’ll inspect .github/workflows/integration-test.yml first, specifically the integration-test job lines 18–64. It fails only on the shared runner, so the runner image, service containers, and environment flags are the likely divergence. I want to see whether the workflow uses ubuntu-latest or a pinned 24.04 image, whether Postgres/Redis are declared with health checks or just port mappings, and whether CI=true, NODE_ENV=test, or DEBUG=payment-service is set. The test file references waitForDatabaseReady() at src/integration/payment-service.test.ts:42, so if the workflow lacks a readiness probe or reuses cached node_modules with a stale @testcontainers/core version, the suite can time out on a noisy runner. If the workflow looks identical to local CI, I’ll move to the test harness config next.

My current hypothesis is that the failure is not random test logic but a shared-runner resource race around the ephemeral Docker volume used by integration_test_auth_flow in tests/integration/auth.spec.ts:214. On the shared runner, CI_DOCKER_HOST points to /var/run/docker.sock and the compose file starts postgres:15 with named volume pg_data; unlike isolated runners, containers from a prior job can linger until the cleanup step at .github/workflows/ci.yml:88, leaving port 5432 or the volume in use. If the failing runs show a stale container or occupied port/volume immediately before the flaky test, that confirms the environment race rather than a nondeterministic test dependency.
